bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client dependency / customer concentration — Client dependency is named by management as one of the key risks the ERM program focuses on. The client base is 178 accounts, weighted toward large Fortune 2000 enterprises, so the loss or downsizing of a major account is a structural exposure for an IT services firm of this scale.
- Cybersecurity, data security and privacy — Cybersecurity threats and data security are explicitly listed among the key risks the Enterprise Risk Management program addresses. Zensar operates inside clients' complex, large-scale IT environments and serves banking, insurance, healthcare and public-sector customers where a breach would carry contractual, regulatory and reputational consequences.
- Technology disruption from AI — Management flags advancements in Artificial Intelligence as an emerging risk it evaluates. The same AI wave that Zensar is monetising can compress traditional application-management and infrastructure revenue pools and reset pricing toward outcome-based models.
- Talent availability and attrition — Talent management is an explicitly evaluated risk area. The BRSR turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 26.80% in FY2025-26 from 24.90% in FY2024-25 (26.90% male, 26.60% female), a structural cost and delivery-continuity pressure in a people-led business.
- Geographic and export concentration — Exports contribute 88% of turnover for the Indian entity and revenue is concentrated in North America, Europe and South Africa, leaving earnings exposed to client-country demand cycles, immigration/trade policy and currency movement. The cautionary statement specifically names foreign exchange fluctuations and global economic conditions as factors that can cause actual outcomes to vary.
- Single-activity business concentration — 100% of turnover comes from a single main activity — IT services and solutions — with Digital Application Services at 78% and Cloud Infrastructure and Security at 22%, so there is no non-IT earnings buffer against an IT-spend downturn.
- Macroeconomic, geopolitical and policy volatility — Management's ERM focuses on market fluctuations and financial challenges, and the cautionary statement enumerates changes in government policies, global economic conditions, foreign exchange fluctuations and natural disasters as factors that may cause actual results to differ materially. Rising trade protectionism, US tariffs and the Russia-Ukraine and West Asia conflicts are cited as having affected sentiment, supply chains and economic stability.
- Climate change and ESG/climate-related risk — Climate change is named among the key risks addressed by the ERM program, and ESG/climate-related risks are one of the explicit risk categories assessed alongside strategic, operational, cybersecurity and financial risk. Energy and emission management is carried as a material responsible-business-conduct issue.
- Vertical demand mix — TMT weakness — Management notes that while Financial Services and Insurance saw strong momentum in FY26, Telecommunications, Media and Technology faced headwinds — a reminder that vertical concentration can offset gains elsewhere.

outlook.body:
- Transform into an AI-native enterprise — embedding AI across every dimension of the business, from client delivery to internal operations and talent development, and systematically shifting to a delivery model where AI is embedded in every engagement
- Industrialize AI adoption across service lines through ZenseAI, the next-generation agentic AI platform launched in FY26, and build enterprise-grade capabilities spanning agentic AI, automation and advanced analytics
- Sharpen industry focus (verticalization) and refine go-to-market, with a GTM strategy pivoting around delivering measurable client outcomes and outcome-based engagement
- 'Experience-led Everything' client-centricity strategy under the 'One Zensar' value framework — moving from execution vendor to co-innovation and long-term partner of choice
- Sales transformation through deeper client engagement, client mining and stronger account development
- Operational excellence — lean delivery practices, reusable assets, integrated engagement models and platform-based delivery to lower total cost of ownership and improve efficiency, quality and cost management
- Talent transformation — structured, multilevel AI upskilling programs and continuous learning to build a skilled, agile, AI-fluent workforce and a people-first culture
- Align service offerings to client cost take-out, simplification and productivity improvement using AI-native automation frameworks and cloud optimization services
- Expand delivery footprint closer to clients — opening the technology delivery and engineering centre in Serbia to strengthen the European presence
- Sustainable operations and ESG stewardship — accelerating renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency and responsible facilities management across global operations
- Zensar returns cash to shareholders through dividends governed by a Dividend Distribution Policy adopted in line with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and published on the Company's website. For FY2025-26 the Board declared an interim dividend and has recommended a final dividend, taking the full-year payout above the prior year's level, with the interim payment to be confirmed and the final dividend declared at the 63rd AGM (July 30, 2026). The Board does not propose to transfer any amount to general reserves, choosing instead to retain the entire profit for the year in the profit and loss account. The Company has not accepted any public deposits and has not given any loans to any parties under Section 186; investments and guarantees are disclosed in the notes. Related-party dealings are stated to be in the ordinary course of business and at arm's length, with omnibus Audit Committee approval for repetitive transactions, specific approval otherwise, and prior Member approval for material related party transactions — the 63rd AGM seeks such approval for transactions with step-down subsidiary Zensar (South Africa) Pty Ltd for FY2026-27. Reinvestment intent, per the value-creation model, is directed at delivery centers, IT infrastructure, emerging markets, R&D, AI platforms and accelerators, and energy-efficiency/renewable-energy initiatives.
- Energy and emission management is the company's identified material responsible-business-conduct issue and is treated as an opportunity: real-time monitoring of energy consumption, identification of opportunities to reduce energy wastage across operations, and a stated direction of increasing the share of renewable energy in global electricity consumption to support emissions reduction
- Employee and partner engagement through communication, awareness initiatives and collaborative solution development to embed responsible resource management across the organization
- BRSR disclosures are made on a consolidated basis and BRSR Core carries reasonable assurance from an external provider, BSI Group India Pvt. Ltd.
- A published Grievance Redressal Policy and grievance mechanism is in place for all six stakeholder groups — communities, investors (other than shareholders), shareholders, employees and workers, customers, and value chain partners/vendors
- Diversity: women are 30.16% of permanent employees and 29.66% of total employees, with female representation on the Board of Directors at 12.50%; differently abled employees are tracked for the Indian entity based on voluntary disclosure
- Workforce retention is disclosed and tracked: permanent-employee turnover rate of 26.80% in FY2025-26 versus 24.90% in FY2024-25 and 24.70% in FY2023-24 (including both voluntary and involuntary attrition)
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
- A dedicated sustainability contact is designated for BRSR queries (sustainability@zensar.com), indicating an owned ESG reporting function
- The Enterprise Risk Management program formally covers ESG/climate-related risks alongside strategic, operational, cybersecurity and financial risks, using both top-down and bottom-up assessment
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Zensar is an asset-light IT services company, so expansion in FY26 took the form of delivery footprint, platform build-out and capability investment rather than plant capacity. The single named physical expansion of the year was the opening of a technology delivery and engineering centre in Serbia, described by the Chairman as a milestone that strengthens the company's presence in Europe and brings engineering capabilities closer to clients. On the platform side, Zensar launched ZenseAI, a proprietary next-generation agentic AI platform, and expanded its AI, cloud and digital engineering capabilities; the value-creation model states that financial capital drives investments in delivery centers, IT infrastructure and emerging markets to support delivery scalability, and funds investments in R&D, AI platforms and accelerators as well as energy efficiency and renewable-energy adoption. The group operated through 15 subsidiaries as of March 31, 2026, providing digital solutions and technology services globally. The Board's Report records no change in the nature of business during the year and states there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position between March 31, 2026 and the date of the report; no new plant, capacity or dated capex project is disclosed.

outlook.body:
- AI has moved from experimentation to enterprise-scale adoption and is now a boardroom priority linked to cost optimization, productivity improvement and long-term growth; AI is becoming a key differentiator in deal wins
- Clients are consolidating vendors and directing spend toward partners who can deliver measurable business outcomes from AI
- Enterprises remain in a cautious macroeconomic environment prioritizing cost rationalization, vendor consolidation and productivity improvement, with discretionary technology spends under pressure and spending focused on rapid ROI, operational efficiency and resilience
- Financial Services and Insurance (FSI) saw strong momentum during FY26 while Telecommunications, Media and Technology (TMT) faced headwinds
- Cloud Infrastructure and Security is seeing strong industry tailwinds, growing materially faster than Digital and Application Services
- Rest of the World was the fastest-growing geography while the United States remained the largest contributor
- Industry-level outlook: global IT spending projected to grow about 10.8% in 2026 with IT services expanding around 8.7%, and the Indian IT sector estimated to grow 6.1% YoY in FY26 (Gartner / NASSCOM cited by management)
- Industry strategies are expected to consolidate around core strengths, with differentiation driven by platform-led models, a transition from services to solutions, outcome-based pricing and selective M&A underpinned by AI-first delivery
- Management remains mindful of ongoing macroeconomic volatility, inflationary pressures and an evolving trade and regulatory landscape, but says it is well prepared to help clients navigate uncertainty and manage costs
- Profitability improvement attributed to operational efficiencies and favourable currency movement
- Order book, profitability and cash position collectively reached the strongest levels in Zensar's history (MD & CEO's message)
- Closed the largest deal in Zensar's history during FY26, described as affirming the maturity of solution capabilities and deepening client trust
- About 36.4% of the order book is influenced by AI, supported by multiple high-value, AI-led wins that scaled AI-native offerings to enterprise-level adoption
- FY26 performance described as resilient and supported by disciplined execution, which strengthened profitability, order book and cash reserves

deepdive.thesis: Zensar delivered resilient Q1FY26 revenue growth of 1.9% CC and a healthy $172M order book, driven by AI-infused deals (20% of bookings) and improved utilization, but margins faced near-term pressure from $3M Q2 wage hikes and pending ESOP, making execution on AI-led productivity and margin recovery the key differentiator.

open.item: The Board recommends a final dividend of INR 12.60 per share (face value INR 2.00) taking the total FY2025-26 dividend to INR 15.00 per share (750%), against INR 13.00 per share (650%) in the previous year.
The Company remains committed to becoming an AI-native technology services company, having launched the proprietary agentic AI platform ZenseAI to embed intelligence across every engagement.
The Company will continue building future-ready talent through initiatives such as the Ignite AI Academy, which has already trained over 9,200 employees with more than 12,500 AI course completions.

Business strategy is anchored on six stated pillars: client-first culture, sales transformation (client mining and building scale), verticalization and go-to-market transformation, operational excellence, talent transformation, and sustainable operations.
Zensar will continue advancing its AI-native capabilities and maintain disciplined execution while deepening the value delivered to clients.
The company will continue to invest in its people-first culture and ESG agenda as foundational to long-term value creation.
Management flags ongoing macroeconomic volatility, inflationary pressures, an evolving trade and regulatory landscape, and discretionary technology spends under pressure as watch items.

Financial capital is to be deployed into delivery centers, IT infrastructure and emerging markets, and into R&D, AI platforms and accelerators, to support delivery scalability and differentiated offerings.

risks.note: Client dependency is named by management as one of the key risks the ERM program focuses on. The client base is 178 accounts, weighted toward large Fortune 2000 enterprises, so the loss or downsizing of a major account is a structural exposure for an IT services firm of this scale.

Cybersecurity threats and data security are explicitly listed among the key risks the Enterprise Risk Management program addresses. Zensar operates inside clients' complex, large-scale IT environments and serves banking, insurance, healthcare and public-sector customers where a breach would carry contractual, regulatory and reputational consequences.

Management flags advancements in Artificial Intelligence as an emerging risk it evaluates. The same AI wave that Zensar is monetising can compress traditional application-management and infrastructure revenue pools and reset pricing toward outcome-based models.

Talent management is an explicitly evaluated risk area. The BRSR turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 26.80% in FY2025-26 from 24.90% in FY2024-25 (26.90% male, 26.60% female), a structural cost and delivery-continuity pressure in a people-led business.

Exports contribute 88% of turnover for the Indian entity and revenue is concentrated in North America, Europe and South Africa, leaving earnings exposed to client-country demand cycles, immigration/trade policy and currency movement. The cautionary statement specifically names foreign exchange fluctuations and global economic conditions as factors that can cause actual outcomes to vary.

100% of turnover comes from a single main activity — IT services and solutions — with Digital Application Services at 78% and Cloud Infrastructure and Security at 22%, so there is no non-IT earnings buffer against an IT-spend downturn.

Management's ERM focuses on market fluctuations and financial challenges, and the cautionary statement enumerates changes in government policies, global economic conditions, foreign exchange fluctuations and natural disasters as factors that may cause actual results to differ materially. Rising trade protectionism, US tariffs and the Russia-Ukraine and West Asia conflicts are cited as having affected sentiment, supply chains and economic stability.

Climate change is named among the key risks addressed by the ERM program, and ESG/climate-related risks are one of the explicit risk categories assessed alongside strategic, operational, cybersecurity and financial risk. Energy and emission management is carried as a material responsible-business-conduct issue.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AI has moved from experimentation to enterprise-scale adoption and is now a boardroom priority linked to cost optimization, productivity improvement and long-term growth; AI is becoming a key differentiator in deal wins
- Clients are consolidating vendors and directing spend toward partners who can deliver measurable business outcomes from AI
- Enterprises remain in a cautious macroeconomic environment prioritizing cost rationalization, vendor consolidation and productivity improvement, with discretionary technology spends under pressure and spending focused on rapid ROI, operational efficiency and resilience
- Financial Services and Insurance (FSI) saw strong momentum during FY26 while Telecommunications, Media and Technology (TMT) faced headwinds
- Cloud Infrastructure and Security is seeing strong industry tailwinds, growing materially faster than Digital and Application Services
- Rest of the World was the fastest-growing geography while the United States remained the largest contributor
- Industry-level outlook: global IT spending projected to grow about 10.8% in 2026 with IT services expanding around 8.7%, and the Indian IT sector estimated to grow 6.1% YoY in FY26 (Gartner / NASSCOM cited by management)
- Industry strategies are expected to consolidate around core strengths, with differentiation driven by platform-led models, a transition from services to solutions, outcome-based pricing and selective M&A underpinned by AI-first delivery
- Management remains mindful of ongoing macroeconomic volatility, inflationary pressures and an evolving trade and regulatory landscape, but says it is well prepared to help clients navigate uncertainty and manage costs
- Profitability improvement attributed to operational efficiencies and favourable currency movement
- Order book, profitability and cash position collectively reached the strongest levels in Zensar's history (MD & CEO's message)
- Closed the largest deal in Zensar's history during FY26, described as affirming the maturity of solution capabilities and deepening client trust
- About 36.4% of the order book is influenced by AI, supported by multiple high-value, AI-led wins that scaled AI-native offerings to enterprise-level adoption

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Zensar is an asset-light IT services company, so expansion in FY26 took the form of delivery footprint, platform build-out and capability investment rather than plant capacity. The single named physical expansion of the year was the opening of a technology delivery and engineering centre in Serbia, described by the Chairman as a milestone that strengthens the company's presence in Europe and brings engineering capabilities closer to clients. On the platform side, Zensar launched ZenseAI, a proprietary next-generation agentic AI platform, and expanded its AI, cloud and digital engineering capabilities; the value-creation model states that financial capital drives investments in delivery centers, IT infrastructure and emerging markets to support delivery scalability, and funds investments in R&D, AI platforms and accelerators as well as energy efficiency and renewable-energy adoption. The group operated through 15 subsidiaries as of March 31, 2026, providing digital solutions and technology services globally. The Board's Report records no change in the nature of business during the year and states there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position between March 31, 2026 and the date of the report; no new plant, capacity or dated capex project is disclosed.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
